summary: Proposes a new top-level MIME content type called model, to extend the types defined in the first MIME document, so email can carry things like 3D models.

eli5.summary: This adds a new kind of item for email, so people can send 3D shapes and the like.

questions: what is the mime model type
how to send 3d models by email
how are unknown model subtypes handled
subtitle: A proposed new top-level MIME type, model, for 3D shapes, meshes and other structured models.

tldr.problem: Models such as CAD drawings, 3D scenes and computational meshes did not fit the existing MIME primary types, and conversions between them lose less information than conversions to other kinds of content.
tldr.mechanism: It defines a new primary type, model, for multidimensional structures with physical scaling and relationships between their parts. Individual subtypes such as model/iges, model/vrml and model/mesh are left to separate documents.
tldr.outcome: Unrecognized subtypes are treated as application/octet-stream, and model data is assumed to be binary and sent as base64 in email. The RFC is a Proposed Standard that has been updated by RFC 9141.

today: RFC 2077 is a Proposed Standard that has been updated by RFC 9141, and it has not been obsoleted. The RFC itself says the subtypes would be registered under separate documents.

sections.title: Proposing a Model Content Type
sections.content:
The memo proposes an update to RFC 2045 that adds a new primary content type, model. RFC 2045 describes how message bodies are labeled with type and subtype pairs. The authors argue that models are a fundamental kind of content with their own presentation, hardware and processing needs.

This document does not define subtypes. It describes what a model is, gives examples and explains the benefit of grouping models together. The authors call it a discussion document for an agreed definition, intended to become an accepted extension to RFC 2045. Its audience includes developers of input/output filters, viewer software and hardware, MIME transport and decoders.
sections.eli5: The authors want email to have a new category, like adding a shelf for 3D things in a library that only had shelves for books, pictures and music.

sections.title: What Counts as a Model
sections.content:
A model is defined as an electronically exchangeable behavioral or physical representation within a given domain. Loosely, models are multidimensional structures made of one or more objects. When there are several objects, one primary object defines the arrangement and relationships of the others, much as multipart/related does in email. The RFC says model types describe how something behaves, in contrast to typical data types that describe how something is.

In detail, a model has these properties:

  • Three or more dimensions forming an orthogonal system.
  • A structural relationship between its elements.
  • Scaling or calibration factors tied to physical units such as force, time or size.
  • One object or a collection of objects arranged around a reference object.

The text adds assumptions. The default dimensionality is spatial and temporal. Models contain underlying structure that may not be directly visible to the user. Conversion between model domains is assumed to be lossless. Grouping them means conversion between model subtypes loses less information than conversion to subtypes of other primary types. The RFC compares this to grouping images and video, noting that converting a GIF image to a JPEG image loses less than converting it to an AU audio file.
sections.eli5: A model is a thing that remembers its shape, size and how its parts fit together, like a toy car whose wheels stay attached in the right places no matter how you turn it.

sections.title: Optional Parameters
sections.content:
The formal template for a model subtype lists no required parameters and two optional ones, shown for illustration only and to be covered in detail by each subtype: a number of dimensions, used as a hint when selecting viewer programs, and state. The text names the first parameter dimensionality in one place and dimension in another, so the exact spelling is left to subtypes.

The state parameter is static or dynamic. In a static model the observer may translate, rotate, pan or zoom but the data does not change. In a dynamic model the data itself is manipulated, for example by skews, elongations or scales. The list of parameters does not limit what a subtype may define.
sections.eli5: A model can carry little hints: how many dimensions it has, and whether you can only look at it (static) or also squish and stretch it (dynamic).

sections.title: Encoding and Transport
sections.content:
Unrecognized model subtypes should at a minimum be treated as application/octet-stream. Implementations may also pass them to a general-purpose model viewer if one is available.

Subtypes may be textual or binary. Unless a subtype's registration says otherwise, model data is assumed to be binary, which implies base64 encoding for email and binary transfer for ftp and http. The registration template recommends base64 for sending model/* documents through MIME electronic mail. The RFC's example header uses Content-Type: model/mesh; dimension="4"; state="static" with Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64.
sections.eli5: If a program does not know what kind of model it got, it treats it like an unknown package and keeps it safe, or hands it to a viewer that might understand it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC states that model data files are read-only and do not contain file system modifiers or batch or macro commands. The data is not self-modifying, though it may contain interrelationships.

Two cautions follow. A file may carry a default view added by the author, which can change viewer variables, look angle, lighting or visualization options, and can involve computing values for display. For motorized equipment it may move the hardware from its rest state to the object's starting orientation. Also, the internal structure of a file may direct agents to fetch more data from the network, and the security limits of those inclusions are not presupposed. Further comments are left to each subtype's registration.
sections.eli5: A model file is like a statue, not a robot: it does not rewrite itself. But it might say how to show itself, or point to other files, so a viewer should be careful.

sections.title: Expected Subtypes
sections.content:
The RFC lists subtypes it expects but does not register them. They are model/iges, model/vrml and model/mesh. IGES was already registered as application/iges, and its author, who is also an author of this memo, expected to re-register it as model/iges at the appropriate time.

The appendices describe each community. VRML is described as not proprietary to any one vendor. Meshes come from finite element and finite difference simulations and are composed of a large number of simple objects with implicit connectivity. IGES is a neutral format for exchanging CAD data between systems. The appendices also list example hardware that could process such data, such as stereo glasses, 3D lithography machines and milling machines.
sections.eli5: The authors name three kinds of model they expect to come first: a 3D CAD drawing, a 3D web scene and a simulation mesh. Each gets its own paperwork later.

viz.caption: EXAMPLE MESSAGE HEADER FROM THE RFC

data.title: Model data in email
data.code:
To:   you@some.org
From: nelson18@llnl.gov
Date: Fri, 30 Aug 96 13:33:19 -0700
Content-Type: model/mesh; dimension="4"; state="static"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64
MIME-Version: 1.0
Subject: model data file
